vault_has_bindings.action: Disconnect the websites first, or remove the vault together with its connections (an administrator can do this). Nothing changes on the websites themselves.

version_not_deployable.title: Version cannot be deployed
version_not_deployable.cause: Alice has not read the details of this version yet, or the version belongs to another certificate.
version_not_deployable.action: Use Check now on the vault's page, then try again.

held_needs_admin.title: An administrator must deploy this version
held_needs_admin.cause: This version is waiting for an administrator: the license was not available at some point since the version appeared, or its certificate chain is incomplete. Only an administrator may deploy it.
held_needs_admin.action: Ask an administrator to deploy it from the certificate's page.

import_confirm_needed.title: Name already used in the vault
import_confirm_needed.cause: The vault already has a certificate with this name. Importing adds a new version to it and can replace its settings, including its own renewal in Key Vault.
import_confirm_needed.action: Confirm that Alice should add a new version to the existing certificate, or choose another name.

import_in_progress.title: Import already running
import_in_progress.cause: An import under this name into this vault has not finished yet, or its result is not confirmed yet.
import_in_progress.action: Wait until it has finished. Alice shows the result on the vault's page.

import_rejected.title: Key Vault refused the import
import_rejected.cause: The vault refused the certificate, so nothing was created in it.
import_rejected.action: Check that the certificate is valid and comes with its private key, and ask your Azure administrator whether the vault accepts imports from Alice. If it keeps happening, give your administrator the request ID shown here.

import_outcome_unknown.title: Import outcome unknown
import_outcome_unknown.cause: Alice sent the certificate to the vault but never learned whether the vault accepted it, and no later check of the vault showed it (or the vault was removed in the meantime).
import_outcome_unknown.action: Open the vault in Azure and look for the certificate. If it is not there, import it again.

client_certificate_invalid.title: Sign-in certificate not usable
client_certificate_invalid.cause: The certificate Alice signs in with must come with an RSA private key of at least 2048 bits.
client_certificate_invalid.action: Use a certificate with an RSA key of 2048 bits or more that is registered with the application in Azure.

vault_duplicate.title: Vault already added
vault_duplicate.cause: Alice already has a vault with this address, or a vault or server with this name.
vault_duplicate.action: Choose another name, or open the vault or server that already has it.

import_name_exists.title: A certificate with this name exists in the vault
import_name_exists.cause: When Alice sent the import, the vault already had a certificate with this name, so nothing was imported.
import_name_exists.action: Use Check now on the vault's page, then import again and confirm that a new version may be added, or choose another name.

import_invalid.title: Certificate cannot be imported
import_invalid.cause: Alice could not prepare this certificate for Key Vault: its name, its key or its file is outside what Key Vault accepts, or the certificate changed in Alice after the import was requested. Nothing was sent.
import_invalid.action: Use a name of letters, digits and hyphens (up to 127 characters), and a certificate with an RSA or ECDSA private key, then try again.

binding_gone.title: Website is no longer connected
binding_gone.cause: The website was disconnected from this vault certificate before the deployment started, so nothing was deployed.
binding_gone.action: Connect the website again if it should follow the certificate.

auto_deploy_off.title: Automatic deployment was switched off
auto_deploy_off.cause: Automatic deployment of this certificate was switched off before this deployment started, so nothing was deployed.
auto_deploy_off.action: Use Deploy now for this version. Switching automatic deployment on again applies only to versions Alice finds afterwards.

vault_unavailable.title: Vault is disabled or removed
vault_unavailable.cause: The vault is disabled or was removed from Alice, so Alice cannot read its certificate.
vault_unavailable.action: Check the vault's status in Alice, or add the vault again.

version_held.title: Version is held
version_held.cause: This version is held until an administrator releases it, so it is not deployed automatically.
version_held.action: An administrator can deploy it from the certificate's page.

version_not_held.title: Version is not held
version_not_held.cause: This version is not held, so there is nothing to release.
version_not_held.action: Reload the page to see the version's current state.

version_superseded.title: A newer version replaced this one
version_superseded.cause: A newer version of the certificate was found before this deployment started, so nothing was deployed.
version_superseded.action: If automatic deployment is on, Alice deploys the newer version by itself. Otherwise use Deploy now.

wave_stopped.title: Automatic deployment of this version was stopped
wave_stopped.cause: Three deployments of this version failed, so Alice stopped deploying it automatically. This deployment sent nothing.
wave_stopped.action: Fix the cause shown on the failed deployments, then use Deploy now.

import_vault_deleted.title: Vault was removed before the import was sent
import_vault_deleted.cause: The vault was removed from Alice while this import was waiting, so nothing was sent.
import_vault_deleted.action: Add the vault again if you still want to import the certificate into it.

import_cancelled.title: Import cancelled before it was sent
import_cancelled.cause: The task that would have sent this import ended before it sent anything (it was cancelled, failed or is gone), so nothing was sent.

import_admin_required.title: The person who requested the import is no longer an administrator
import_admin_required.cause: Importing a certificate into a vault moves its private key out of Alice, so only an administrator may do it. The person who asked for this import is no longer an administrator, so nothing was sent.
import_admin_required.action: An administrator can request the import again.

credential_unreadable.title: Alice cannot read this vault's stored credentials
credential_unreadable.cause: The sign-in credentials Alice stored for this vault cannot be decrypted with Alice's current master key (the key was replaced, or the stored data was damaged). Nothing was read from the vault. Nothing was changed on your servers.
credential_unreadable.action: Open the vault's page, choose Replace credentials and enter the vault's sign-in details again, then deploy again.

running.title: Another backup is being made.
running.cause: A backup started by the daily schedule, by another administrator or on the server with alicectl is still being written. Alice makes one backup at a time.
running.action: Wait a few minutes until it has finished, then try again.

not_configured.title: Backups are not set up yet.
not_configured.cause: No recovery passphrase has been set, so Alice has no key to encrypt backups with.
not_configured.action: Set the recovery passphrase in the setup wizard. Backups start after that.

not_found.title: This backup was not found.
not_found.cause: No backup file with this name is in the backups directory. It may have been removed by the retention rule or by hand.
not_found.action: Reload the list of backups and choose a file that is listed.

write_failed.title: The backup could not be written.
write_failed.cause: The backups directory is full or not writable, or the disk reported an error. Alice removed the incomplete file; no backup was made.
write_failed.action: Free disk space in the backups directory (the Backups tab shows the free space), then back up again. If it keeps failing, send Alice's log to support.

provider_unreachable.title: The certificate authority could not be reached.
provider_unreachable.cause: Alice could not connect to the certificate authority. The network, a firewall or the authority itself may be unavailable. Nothing was issued.
provider_unreachable.action: Check that this server can reach the authority's address, then try again later.

directory_invalid.title: The address is not a certificate authority.
directory_invalid.cause: The address answered, but not in the way an ACME certificate authority does, so Alice cannot use it.
directory_invalid.action: Check the address of the directory in the provider settings. Your authority's documentation lists it.

terms_not_accepted.title: The terms of service have not been accepted.
terms_not_accepted.cause: The certificate authority requires its terms of service to be accepted before an account can be created.
terms_not_accepted.action: Read the terms shown for this authority and confirm them when you register the account.

account_rejected.title: The authority rejected the account.
account_rejected.cause: The certificate authority did not accept the account details, for example the external account binding (key identifier and key) or the contact address.
account_rejected.action: Check the key identifier and key that your authority gave you, and the contact address, then register again.

ca_rate_limited.title: The authority is limiting requests.
ca_rate_limited.cause: The certificate authority has temporarily refused more requests from this installation, or for these names. Alice will try again later.
ca_rate_limited.action: Wait. The authority states when requests are accepted again; ordering sooner only makes the wait longer.

validation_failed_dns.title: The DNS proof failed.
validation_failed_dns.cause: The authority could not find the expected proof record in the DNS zone, so it did not confirm that you control the name.
validation_failed_dns.action: Check that the DNS hook adds the record to the right zone and that the name servers answer, then order again.

validation_failed_http.title: The web proof failed.
validation_failed_http.cause: The authority could not fetch the proof file from the server for this name, so it did not confirm that you control the name.
validation_failed_http.action: Check that the name points to the right server and that port 80 reaches it, then order again.

hook_refused.title: The DNS hook refused the request.
hook_refused.cause: The DNS hook that adds the proof record did not accept Alice's request, so the authority could not check the name.
hook_refused.action: Check the hook's address and secret in Settings and its own log, then order again.

identifier_refused.title: The authority will not issue for this name.
identifier_refused.cause: The certificate authority refused one of the names, for example because it is not a public name or it is on a block list.
identifier_refused.action: Remove the name from the certificate or choose an authority that issues for it.

not_issued_in_time.title: The certificate was not issued in time.
not_issued_in_time.cause: The authority did not finish the order within the time Alice waits, so no certificate was received. Alice can try again.
not_issued_in_time.action: Order again later. If it keeps happening, ask the authority whether it is having problems.

key_policy_not_allowed.title: The key type is not allowed.
key_policy_not_allowed.cause: The certificate authority does not accept the kind of key chosen for this certificate.
key_policy_not_allowed.action: Choose a key type that your authority supports, for example ECDSA P-256 or RSA 2048.

provider_in_use.title: The authority is still in use.
provider_in_use.cause: Certificates still use this certificate authority, so it cannot be removed.
provider_in_use.action: Delete these certificates first, or move them to another authority, then remove this one.

tls_trust_failed.title: The authority's connection is not trusted.
tls_trust_failed.cause: Alice reached the certificate authority but could not trust its secure connection. Nothing was sent.
tls_trust_failed.action: If your authority uses its own root certificate, add it to the provider settings. Never turn the check off.

rollover_unsupported.title: The authority cannot change the account key.
rollover_unsupported.cause: This certificate authority does not support replacing an account key. The account was not changed.
rollover_unsupported.action: Register a new account at this authority and move the certificates to it.

name_not_allowed.title: This name is not allowed.
name_not_allowed.cause: The name is not on the list of names this certificate authority or DNS hook may issue for. Nothing was ordered.
name_not_allowed.action: An Administrator can add the domain ending to the allowed names of the provider and the hook, or you can use a different name.

order_running.title: An order is already running.
order_running.cause: This certificate is already being ordered, so a second order is not started and what the order uses cannot change. A key change of a certificate authority's account also waits while any certificate of that authority is being ordered.
order_running.action: Wait until the running order finishes (its result appears on the certificate), then try again.

challenge_unavailable.title: This proof method cannot be used here.
challenge_unavailable.cause: The web proof (HTTP-01) cannot prove these names on this server: it cannot prove a wildcard name, and it needs a server that Alice manages as an Nginx server. Nothing was changed.
challenge_unavailable.action: Choose the DNS proof, or choose an Nginx server that answers for these names on port 80.

key_type_locked.title: The key type cannot be changed.
key_type_locked.cause: This certificate is already deployed to servers with its current key type. Changing it would break those deployments. Nothing was changed.
key_type_locked.action: Create a new certificate with the other key type and move the deployments to it.

hook_in_use.title: The DNS hook is still in use.
hook_in_use.cause: Certificates still publish their DNS proof through this hook, so it cannot be removed. Nothing was changed.
hook_in_use.action: Delete these certificates or switch them to another hook first, then remove this one.

name_taken.title: This name is already used.
name_taken.cause: Another certificate authority or DNS hook already has this name. Nothing was saved.

account_exists.title: This authority already has an account.
account_exists.cause: Alice keeps one account per certificate authority, and this one already has an active account. No new account was created.
account_exists.action: Use the existing account. To start over, deactivate it first and then register again.

directory_change_unconfirmed.title: Changing the address needs your confirmation.
directory_change_unconfirmed.cause: This certificate authority has an active account. A new directory address usually means a different authority, where that account does not exist. Nothing was changed.
directory_change_unconfirmed.action: Check the address. If it is right, confirm the change: the current account is then retired and you register a new one.

account_state.title: The account cannot do this now.
account_state.cause: The account is retired, deactivated or still being changed, so this action does not apply to it. Nothing was changed.
account_state.action: Refresh the page and use the authority's current active account.

rollover_pending.title: The account key change is not finished.
rollover_pending.cause: Another change of this account is still running, or Alice asked the certificate authority to change the account key and the answer did not arrive, so it is not yet known which key the authority uses.
rollover_pending.action: Wait a moment and try again. If a key change is waiting, use "Check key change" to let Alice ask the authority again; nothing else changes until it is settled.

secret_unreadable.title: A stored secret cannot be read.
secret_unreadable.cause: A secret Alice keeps for this authority or hook (an account key, an external account key or a hook secret) cannot be decrypted with the current master key, for example after a restore with another key.
secret_unreadable.action: Restore the matching master key, or enter the secret again (for an account: register a new account).

order_abandoned.title: The interrupted certificate request was abandoned.
order_abandoned.cause: Alice was stopped (or lost its job) while it asked the certificate authority for this certificate, and the request could not be finished afterwards: the authority had not issued the certificate yet. Nothing was stored and the prepared private key was deleted.
order_abandoned.action: Request the certificate again. Any proof records that were still published are removed automatically.

not_issued.title: This certificate has not been issued yet.
not_issued.cause: The certificate authority has not issued a certificate for these names yet, so there is nothing to connect to a website or to deploy.
not_issued.action: Get the certificate first (Get certificate now on its page), then connect the websites or deploy it.

location_bound.title: This website already follows another certificate.
location_bound.cause: A website can follow only one certificate: this one is already connected to another certificate from a certificate authority or to a certificate in a vault.
location_bound.action: Disconnect the website from the other certificate first, or choose another website.

location_not_bound.title: This website is not connected to this certificate.
location_not_bound.cause: Deploy now puts the certificate only on the websites connected to it, and this website is not one of them.
location_not_bound.action: Connect the website to the certificate first, or leave it out of the selection.

binding_gone.title: The website no longer follows this certificate.
binding_gone.cause: An automatic deployment of a certificate from a certificate authority was waiting to run, but the website was disconnected from the certificate (or the certificate was removed, or the website now follows another certificate). Nothing was sent to the server.
binding_gone.action: Nothing to do if this was intended. Otherwise connect the website to the certificate again and choose Deploy now.

auto_deploy_off.title: Automatic deployment was switched off.
auto_deploy_off.cause: An automatic deployment of a certificate from a certificate authority was waiting to run, but automatic deployment was switched off for the certificate or for this website. Nothing was sent to the server.
auto_deploy_off.action: Nothing to do if this was intended. To put the certificate on the website now, choose Deploy now.

certificate_superseded.title: A newer certificate replaced this one.
certificate_superseded.cause: An automatic deployment was waiting to run, but the certificate authority has issued a newer certificate for these names since. Nothing was sent to the server; Alice deploys the newer certificate instead.
certificate_superseded.action: Nothing to do: the newer certificate is deployed automatically.

deploy_stopped.title: Automatic deployment of this certificate stopped.
deploy_stopped.cause: Three deployments of this certificate failed, so Alice stopped deploying it automatically. A deployment that was still waiting sent nothing to the server.
deploy_stopped.action: Look at the failed deployments, remove the cause, then choose Deploy now.

deploy_held.title: This certificate is waiting for an administrator.
deploy_held.cause: Alice holds this certificate for an administrator before it is deployed automatically (it arrived before the license allowed changes again, or Alice cannot confirm the certificates that vouch for it). A deployment that was waiting sent nothing to the server.
deploy_held.action: An administrator checks the certificate, then chooses Deploy now or releases it for automatic deployment.

no_bindings.title: No website is connected to this certificate yet.
no_bindings.cause: Deploy now puts the certificate on the websites connected to it, and none is connected.
no_bindings.action: Connect at least one website to the certificate, then choose Deploy now again.

too_many_bindings.title: Choose the websites to deploy to.
too_many_bindings.cause: This certificate is connected to more websites than one deployment request can take (at most 20).
too_many_bindings.action: Select the websites to deploy to, at most 20 at a time, and choose Deploy now again.

not_this_certificate.title: This certificate was not issued for this ACME certificate.
not_this_certificate.cause: Only a certificate that an order of this ACME certificate produced can be revoked from its page.
not_this_certificate.action: Choose a version listed under this certificate's orders, or leave the version out to revoke the current certificate.

revoke_unsupported.title: The certificate authority does not offer revocation.
revoke_unsupported.cause: The certificate authority's directory lists no revokeCert address, so Alice cannot ask it to revoke a certificate. Nothing was sent.
revoke_unsupported.action: Revoke the certificate through the certificate authority's own tools, and replace it on your servers.

revoke_reason_refused.title: The certificate authority does not accept this revocation reason.
revoke_reason_refused.cause: Alice sends the reasons a certificate owner may give (unspecified, key compromise, affiliation changed, superseded, cessation of operation); the certificate authority refused the one chosen.
revoke_reason_refused.action: Choose another reason, for example Unspecified, and revoke again.

revoke_unauthorized.title: The certificate authority refused to revoke this certificate.
revoke_unauthorized.cause: The certificate authority says this account may not revoke this certificate: another account ordered it, or the authority does not know it (for example after a change of directory).
revoke_unauthorized.action: Revoke the certificate with the account that ordered it, through the certificate authority's own tools if needed, and replace it on your servers.

already_replaced.title: Another order at the certificate authority is already replacing this certificate.
already_replaced.cause: Alice named the current certificate as the one this renewal replaces, and the certificate authority says another order already does. Alice takes that order over when it is one of its own, or orders once more without naming the certificate; this code appears only when that did not help either.
already_replaced.action: Nothing, usually: the other order ends at the certificate authority within a few days and Alice renews again by itself. If the renewal keeps failing, use Check again and resume on the certificate's page after that time.

scope_too_large.title: This scope is too large to scan.
scope_too_large.cause: A scope may cover at most 4,096 addresses, and one scan at most 20,000 combinations of address, port and server name. IPv6 ranges may be at most a /120. Nothing was saved.
scope_too_large.action: Split the scope into smaller ones, or list fewer ports or server names, then save again.

entry_not_allowed.title: This address may not be scanned.
entry_not_allowed.cause: The address or range is outside the Allowed scan networks, or it is one Alice never scans: its own addresses, the database, loopback, link-local and cloud metadata addresses, or a range in the exclusions. Nothing was saved.
entry_not_allowed.action: Remove the entry, or ask an Administrator to add its network to the Allowed scan networks in the discovery settings.

entry_invalid.title: An entry of this scope is not valid.
entry_invalid.cause: An entry must be an IP address, a network range such as 10.0.0.0/24, or a host name. Ports must be between 1 and 65535 and server names must be plain host names. Nothing was saved.
entry_invalid.action: Correct the marked entry and save again.

scan_running.title: A scan of this scope is already running.
scan_running.cause: Only one scan of a scope runs at a time, so a second one was not started.
scan_running.action: Follow the running scan on the Scans tab. Start a new scan after it has finished.

scan_cancelled.title: The scan was cancelled.
scan_cancelled.cause: Someone cancelled the scan, or Alice stopped it because the license is locked. The results found until then are kept.
scan_cancelled.action: Start the scan again when you need it. If the license is locked, resolve the license first.

scan_timed_out.title: The scan took too long and was stopped.
scan_timed_out.cause: A scan may run for at most 60 minutes. The results found until then are kept.
scan_timed_out.action: Make the scope smaller, or raise its connections per second, then scan again.

too_many_scans.title: Too many scans are running.
too_many_scans.cause: At most two scans run at the same time, so this one was not started.
too_many_scans.action: Wait until one of the running scans has finished, then start this one again.

scope_not_found.title: This scan scope was not found.
scope_not_found.cause: The scope does not exist or it was deleted.
scope_not_found.action: Reload the list of scopes and choose one that is listed.

schedule_invalid.title: The schedule of this scope is not valid.
schedule_invalid.cause: A schedule repeats every 1 to 168 hours. A time window needs a start and an end that differ, and a time zone Alice knows.
schedule_invalid.action: Correct the schedule and save again.

name_unresolved.title: A host name in this scope could not be found.
name_unresolved.cause: Alice asked its name server for the host name and got no address back. Nothing was saved.
name_unresolved.action: Check the spelling of the host name, and check that the server Alice runs on can look it up, then save again.

name_taken.title: A scan scope with this name already exists.
name_taken.cause: Every scope needs its own name.
name_taken.action: Choose a different name and save again.

scan_interrupted.title: The scan was interrupted.
scan_interrupted.cause: Alice restarted, or this installation was restored from a backup, while the scan ran. The results found until then are kept.

scope_disabled.title: This scan scope is switched off.
scope_disabled.cause: A scope that is switched off is not scanned, neither by its schedule nor by hand, so the scan was not started.
scope_disabled.action: Switch the scope on in its settings on the Scopes tab, then start the scan again.

key_mismatch.title: The private key does not belong to the certificate.
key_mismatch.cause: None of the uploaded certificates was made for the uploaded private key. Nothing was changed.
key_mismatch.action: Upload the certificate together with the private key it was issued for.

not_valid_now.title: The certificate is not valid now.
not_valid_now.cause: Its validity has not started yet, has ended, or ends within one day. Nothing was changed.
not_valid_now.action: Upload a certificate that is valid now and for more than one day, or check the server's date and time.

weak_key.title: The certificate's key is not accepted.
weak_key.cause: Alice accepts RSA keys of 2,048 bits or more and ECDSA keys on the P-256 or P-384 curve. Nothing was changed.
weak_key.action: Ask your certificate authority for a certificate with an accepted key type, then upload it.

pfx_password.title: The PFX password is wrong.
pfx_password.cause: The PFX file could not be opened with the password you entered. Nothing was changed.
pfx_password.action: Enter the password the PFX file was exported with, then upload it again.

unreadable.title: The certificate file could not be read.
unreadable.cause: The upload is neither PEM text with the certificate and one unencrypted private key nor a PFX file, or it is larger than 1 MiB. Nothing was changed.
unreadable.action: Upload the certificate and its unencrypted private key as PEM, or a PFX file with its password.

open.title: This certificate already has an open incident.
open.cause: Alice runs one key compromise incident per certificate at a time.
open.action: Open the running incident from the certificate's page and follow it there, or close it first.

state.title: This action does not fit the incident's current step.
state.cause: The incident moved on since the page was loaded, or it is finished.
state.action: Reload the incident and choose one of the actions it offers now.

replacement_invalid.title: This certificate cannot replace the compromised one.
replacement_invalid.cause: A replacement must be a certificate Alice holds the private key of, made with another key, neither revoked nor compromised, and valid now.
replacement_invalid.action: Upload a certificate made with a new private key (or complete a signing request) and choose it as the replacement.

not_revocable.title: Alice cannot revoke this certificate.
not_revocable.cause: Alice revokes only certificates she ordered from a certificate authority (ACME). This certificate came from another source.
not_revocable.action: Ask the certificate authority that issued it to revoke it; Alice has marked it compromised and replaces it on your servers.

other_certificate.title: This place holds another certificate made with the same key.
other_certificate.cause: The file holds a different certificate (other names) that was made with the compromised private key, so Alice did not put this incident's replacement there.
other_certificate.action: Start an incident for that certificate too, from its page, or replace it by hand.

not_deployable.title: Alice cannot deploy to this place.
not_deployable.cause: The file is on a server whose software Alice only discovers, its path or configuration is one Alice cannot change, or it needs a key of another type than the replacement has.
not_deployable.action: Replace the certificate in this file by hand, then scan the server again.

follows_key_vault.title: This place follows a certificate in a key vault.
follows_key_vault.cause: The file is connected to an Azure Key Vault certificate, so a deployment from the incident would be overwritten.
follows_key_vault.action: Replace the certificate in the vault (with a new key); Alice deploys the new version to this place.

follows_other_acme.title: This place follows another certificate from a certificate authority.
follows_other_acme.cause: The file is connected to a different ACME certificate, so a deployment from the incident would be overwritten.
follows_other_acme.action: Start an incident for that certificate too, or disconnect the place and replace it by hand.

location_busy.title: This place stayed busy for too long.
location_busy.cause: Another deployment, a recovery on the server or a server that was not ready kept Alice from deploying the replacement here, many times in a row.
location_busy.action: Check the server and its deployments, then choose Retry on the incident.

deployments_failed.title: The replacement could not be deployed everywhere.
deployments_failed.cause: At least one deployment of the replacement failed. The compromised certificate is not revoked yet, so the places that still serve it keep working.
deployments_failed.action: Look at the failed places and their deployments, fix the cause and choose Retry, or choose Revoke now regardless if the key must be revoked at once.

deployments_unverified.title: Some deployments of the replacement could not be checked.
deployments_unverified.cause: The replacement was deployed, but checking that the server serves it was switched off for some places. Alice revokes the compromised certificate only after every place is checked.
deployments_unverified.action: Check those websites yourself, then choose Revoke now regardless.

key_reused.title: The new certificate uses the compromised key.
key_reused.cause: The certificate chosen as the replacement was made with the same private key as the compromised one, so it is compromised too.
key_reused.action: Order or upload a certificate made with a new private key and choose Retry.

replacement_unusable.title: The replacement certificate can no longer be used.
replacement_unusable.cause: The replacement was revoked, marked compromised, removed, or is no longer valid, or Alice does not hold its private key.
replacement_unusable.action: Order or upload another certificate made with a new private key and choose Retry.

validation.pattern: This value contains characters that are not allowed.
validation.email: Enter a valid email address, for example name@example.com.
validation.host_port: Enter only the server's name or address here. Put the port in the SSH port field.
validation.host_not_allowed: This address cannot be a managed server (it is a link-local, group or broadcast address, or no address at all).
validation.host_ascii: Use the server's plain host name (for international names, the form that starts with xn--) or its IP address.
validation.key_in_certificate: The certificate field contains a private key. Paste only the certificate and its chain here. When you upload a certificate, the private key goes in its own field; for a signing request, Alice already has the key.
validation.duplicate: This value is listed more than once.

email.footer: This message was sent automatically by Alice. Do not reply to it.
email.license_note: Note: Alice's license has expired. Renew it to resume automatic deployment. License page: {{license_url}}
email.license_note_kv:
Note: Alice's license has expired. Renew it to resume automatic deployment. License page: {{license_url}}
Key Vault data may be outdated while the license is expired.

failed.subject: Alice could not make its daily backup
failed.body:
Alice could not make its daily backup at {{time}}. Error: {{error_code}}.

Alice tries again every 5 minutes and does not e-mail again until a backup succeeds. Backups made earlier are kept. Check the Backups tab in Settings and the troubleshooting guide for this error. Open Alice: {{dashboard_url}}

alarm.subject: Alice has had no successful backup for 48 hours
alarm.body:
Alice has not made a successful backup for 48 hours. Last successful backup: {{last_success}}.

Without a recent backup, data changed since then cannot be restored. Fix the cause shown in the Backups tab in Settings, then click Back up now. Open Alice: {{dashboard_url}}

alarm_never.subject: Alice has never made a successful backup
alarm_never.body:
Alice has not made a successful backup since its setup was completed, more than 48 hours ago.

Without a backup, Alice's data cannot be restored. Fix the cause shown in the Backups tab in Settings, then click Back up now. Open Alice: {{dashboard_url}}

test.subject: Alice test e-mail
test.body: This is a test e-mail from Alice. If you received it, Alice can send e-mails with the current mail settings.

certificate_expiring.subject: Certificate expiring: {{name}} (days left: {{days}})

certificate_expired.subject: Certificate expired: {{name}}

kv_certificate_expiring.subject: Key Vault certificate expiring: {{name}} (days left: {{days}})
kv_certificate_expiring.body:
The certificate {{name}} in the Key Vault {{vault}} expires at {{expires_at}}. Days left: {{days}}.

If the vault renews it automatically, Alice deploys the new version where it is connected. Otherwise renew it in Azure before then.

kv_certificate_expired.subject: Key Vault certificate expired: {{name}}
kv_certificate_expired.body:
The certificate {{name}} in the Key Vault {{vault}} expired at {{expires_at}}.

Renew it in Azure; Alice deploys the new version where it is connected.

kv_key_expiring.subject: Key Vault key expiring: {{name}} (days left: {{days}})
kv_key_expiring.body:
The key {{name}} in the Key Vault {{vault}} expires at {{expires_at}}. Days left: {{days}}.

Applications that use this key stop working with it after that time. Create a new key version in Azure before then.

kv_key_expired.subject: Key Vault key expired: {{name}}
kv_key_expired.body:
The key {{name}} in the Key Vault {{vault}} expired at {{expires_at}}.

Create a new key version in Azure and update the applications that use it.

kv_credential_expiring.subject: Key Vault sign-in secret expiring: {{vault}} (days left: {{days}})
kv_credential_expiring.body:
The client secret Alice uses to sign in to the Key Vault {{vault}} expires at {{expires_at}}. Days left: {{days}}.

Create a new client secret in Microsoft Entra ID and enter it on the vault's page in Alice before then. After that time Alice cannot read the vault.

kv_credential_expired.subject: Key Vault sign-in secret expired: {{vault}}
kv_credential_expired.body:
The client secret Alice uses to sign in to the Key Vault {{vault}} expired at {{expires_at}}.

Create a new client secret in Microsoft Entra ID and enter it on the vault's page in Alice.

discovered_certificate_expiring.subject: Certificate not managed by Alice expiring: {{name}} (days left: {{days}})

discovered_certificate_expired.subject: Certificate not managed by Alice expired: {{name}}

more.subject: More expiry notices: {{count}}
more.body:
In this check, {{count}} more items reached an expiry threshold. Alice did not send a separate e-mail for each of them.

Open the Dashboard in Alice to see them all.

more_discovered.subject: More expiry notices for certificates found on the network: {{count}}
more_discovered.body:
In this check, {{count}} more certificates that Alice found on the network, and does not manage, reached an expiry threshold. Alice did not send a separate e-mail for each of them.

See them all on the network discovery page in Alice: {{discovery_url}}

lockout.subject: Sign-in blocked: {{username}}
lockout.body:
After {{failed_logins}} failed sign-in attempts, Alice blocked sign-in for the account {{username}} for {{minutes}} minutes.

If this was not the account's owner, someone may be guessing the password. An administrator can end the block early on the host with the command alice admin unlock.

failed.subject: Certificate deployment failed on {{target_name}}
failed.body:
Alice could not deploy a certificate on the server {{target_name}} (file {{cert_path}}). The server keeps its previous certificate.

The deployment history in Alice shows each step, the reason and what to do. Deployment: {{deployment_id}}

rollback_failed.subject: Manual action needed: certificate restore failed on {{target_name}}
rollback_failed.body:
Alice deployed a certificate on the server {{target_name}} (file {{cert_path}}). The change failed, and the automatic restore failed too.

The previous files are on the server in {{backup_dir}}. Check the website now, then run nginx -t and systemctl status nginx on the server. The deployment history in Alice shows each step. Deployment: {{deployment_id}}

outcome_unknown.subject: Alice could not confirm a certificate deployment on {{target_name}}
outcome_unknown.body:
Alice started deploying a certificate on the server {{target_name}} (file {{cert_path}}), but could not confirm how it ended and has stopped trying.

Check the website now and run nginx -t on the server. If the change reached the server, the previous files are in {{backup_dir}}. The deployment history in Alice shows each step. Deployment: {{deployment_id}}

restored_unverified.subject: The previous certificate is back on {{target_name}} but Alice could not confirm the website serves it
restored_unverified.body:
A certificate deployment on the server {{target_name}} failed (file {{cert_path}}), and Alice put the previous files back. Alice could not confirm that the website serves the previous certificate, for example because another website on this server or a load balancer in front of it answers, or because the check could not connect.

Check the website and run systemctl status nginx on the server. The deployment history in Alice shows each step. Deployment: {{deployment_id}}

superseded.subject: A later operation overwrote the files of a deployment on {{target_name}}
superseded.body:
Alice could not finish or undo a certificate deployment on the server {{target_name}} (file {{cert_path}}) because a later operation has already replaced the files. Alice did not restore anything.

Check which certificate the website serves now, then choose Discover on the server's page in Alice. Deployment: {{deployment_id}}

needs_attention.subject: Alice cannot finish a deployment on {{target_name}}
needs_attention.body:
The connection to the server {{target_name}} was lost during a certificate deployment (file {{cert_path}}), and Alice cannot reach the server to finish or undo it.

Alice tries again every 15 minutes for about a day, then asks for manual action. Until then, check the website and the server's connection. Deployment: {{deployment_id}}

rollback_forbidden.subject: Manual action needed: a failed deployment on {{target_name}} was not undone because the previous certificate is compromised
rollback_forbidden.body:
A certificate deployment on the server {{target_name}} (file {{cert_path}}) failed. Alice did not put the previous files back, because they hold a certificate that was revoked or whose private key is compromised. The files stay as the failed change left them, so the website may not work until another certificate is deployed.

Check the website now. Fix the cause shown in the deployment history in Alice, then deploy a valid certificate again. Do not restore the server's backup of this change by hand: it holds the compromised key. Deployment: {{deployment_id}}

pending_change_restored.subject: Alice put back older certificate files on {{target_name}}; your certificate was not deployed
pending_change_restored.body:
A certificate deployment on the server {{target_name}} (file {{cert_path}}) found an unfinished earlier change of the same files that Alice no longer followed. Alice put back the files from before that earlier change, so the website now serves the certificate from before it. That certificate may be older than the one the website served when the deployment was requested, and it may even have expired. The certificate of this deployment was not written.

Check the website now. Then choose Discover on the server's page in Alice and deploy the certificate again. Earlier change: {{operation_id}}. Deployment: {{deployment_id}}

needs_attention_unconfirmed.subject: Alice cannot confirm a deployment on {{target_name}} yet
needs_attention_unconfirmed.body:
Alice cannot yet confirm how a certificate deployment on the server {{target_name}} ended (file {{cert_path}}): the server did not answer as expected.

Alice tries again every 15 minutes for about a day, then asks for manual action. Until then, check the website. Deployment: {{deployment_id}}

drift_detected.subject: Certificate changed outside Alice on {{target_name}}: {{cert_path}}
drift_detected.body:
The website that uses the file {{cert_path}} on the server {{target_name}} no longer has the certificate it should have ({{certificate_name}}). Alice found {{observed_name}} instead, although the right certificate was there before: someone or another tool changed the file or what the website serves.

Alice did not put the right certificate back by itself.

What to do: open the server in Alice. Its certificate list shows, for this file, the certificate it should have, what Alice last deployed, what the file holds and what the website serves, each with its time. If the change was not intended, choose Repair to deploy the right certificate again. If another tool manages this file, remove the location from the certificate's bindings.

drift_repair_ready.subject: Repair ready: certificate changed outside Alice on {{target_name}}: {{cert_path}}
drift_repair_ready.body:
The website that uses the file {{cert_path}} on the server {{target_name}} no longer has the certificate it should have ({{certificate_name}}). Alice found {{observed_name}} instead, although the right certificate was there before: someone or another tool changed the file or what the website serves.

Alice prepared the repair but does not start it by itself for this location.

What to do: open the server in Alice and check the location. If the change was not intended, choose Repair: Alice deploys the right certificate again, with every check of a deployment. If another tool manages this file, remove the location from the certificate's bindings.

drift_repaired.subject: Certificate put back on {{target_name}}: {{cert_path}}
drift_repaired.body:
The website that uses the file {{cert_path}} on the server {{target_name}} had {{observed_name}} instead of the certificate it should have ({{certificate_name}}). Alice deployed {{certificate_name}} again by itself, and a new check confirmed that the website has it.

If this happens again, find out who changes the file: when Alice has to put the certificate back 3 times within 24 hours, it stops doing so and tells you.

drift_flapping.subject: Alice stopped repairing {{cert_path}} on {{target_name}}: another tool keeps changing it
drift_flapping.body:
Alice put {{certificate_name}} back into the file {{cert_path}} on the server {{target_name}} 3 times within 24 hours, and each time the file was changed again (Alice found {{observed_name}}). Another tool keeps changing this file, and two tools that manage the same file work against each other.

Alice no longer repairs this location by itself: it only reports changes now.

What to do: decide which tool manages this file. If it is Alice, stop the other tool (for example a certbot timer or a configuration management run), then choose automatic repair again on the server's page in Alice. If it is the other tool, remove the location from the certificate's bindings in Alice.

drift_repair_failing.subject: Alice stopped repairing {{cert_path}} on {{target_name}}: the repairs failed
drift_repair_failing.body:
Alice tried 3 times within 24 hours to put {{certificate_name}} back into the file {{cert_path}} on the server {{target_name}} (Alice found {{observed_name}}), and each deployment failed. The deployment history in Alice shows each step and the reason.

Alice no longer repairs this location by itself: it only reports changes now.

What to do: remove the cause shown in the deployment history, then choose Repair, or choose automatic repair again on the server's page in Alice.

host_key_changed.subject: Alice stopped work on a server whose identity changed: {{target_name}}

auth_failed.subject: Alice cannot sign in to a server: {{target_name}}
auth_failed.body:
The server {{target_name}} refused Alice's SSH key.

Check that the user alice-svc still exists on the server and that Alice's public key is in its authorized_keys file. The key and the setup commands are on the Servers page in Alice. Alice tries again at the next scan.

auth_failed.subject: Alice cannot sign in to a Key Vault: {{target_name}}
auth_failed.body:
Alice has failed three times in a row to sign in to the Key Vault {{target_name}}.

The usual causes are a client secret or certificate that has expired or was replaced, an application that was deleted, or a wrong directory. Open the vault in Alice: its page shows the reason and what to do. Replace the credentials there if needed.

Alice keeps trying in the background, at most once an hour, and sign-in works again as soon as the problem is fixed.

certificate_removed.subject: A certificate disappeared from the Key Vault {{target_name}}: {{certificate_name}}
certificate_removed.body:
The certificate {{certificate_name}} is no longer listed in the Key Vault {{target_name}}. Alice keeps its history and marks it as removed.

No website is connected to this certificate in Alice, so nothing else changes.

If the removal was a mistake, recover the certificate in Azure and Alice will show it again at the next check.

certificate_removed_bound.subject: A certificate that websites use disappeared from the Key Vault {{target_name}}: {{certificate_name}}
certificate_removed_bound.body:
The certificate {{certificate_name}} is no longer listed in the Key Vault {{target_name}}. Alice keeps its history and marks it as removed.

Websites are connected to this certificate in Alice. Alice changes nothing on those websites; they keep serving the certificate they have now until it expires, but they will not get a renewal from this certificate.

If the removal was a mistake, recover the certificate in Azure and Alice will show it again at the next check.

certificates_removed_more.subject: More certificates disappeared from the Key Vault {{target_name}}
certificates_removed_more.body:
Alice sent a message for each of the first certificates that disappeared from the Key Vault {{target_name}} in one check. {{count}} more certificates disappeared in the same check and are not listed here. Alice keeps their history and marks them as removed.

Open the vault in Alice to see them all: removed certificates are marked Removed from Key Vault. If this was a mistake, recover the certificates in Azure and Alice will show them again at the next check.

certificates_removed_more_one.subject: Another certificate disappeared from the Key Vault {{target_name}}
certificates_removed_more_one.body:
Alice sent a message for each of the first certificates that disappeared from the Key Vault {{target_name}} in one check. {{count}} more certificate disappeared in the same check and is not listed here. Alice keeps its history and marks it as removed.

Open the vault in Alice to see it: it is marked Removed from Key Vault. If this was a mistake, recover the certificate in Azure and Alice will show it again at the next check.

new_version_available.subject: A new version of {{certificate_name}} was found in the Key Vault {{target_name}}
new_version_available.body:
Alice found a new version of the certificate {{certificate_name}} in the Key Vault {{target_name}}.

Automatic deployment is off for the websites connected to this certificate, so Alice did not deploy it. To deploy it, open the certificate in Alice and choose Deploy now, or switch on automatic deployment.

new_version_held_license.subject: A new version of {{certificate_name}} is waiting for an administrator: Key Vault {{target_name}}
new_version_held_license.body:
Alice found a new version of the certificate {{certificate_name}} in the Key Vault {{target_name}}. Because Alice's license was not available at some point since the version appeared, Alice will not deploy it by itself.

An administrator can open the certificate in Alice and choose Deploy now.

new_version_held_chain.subject: A new version of {{certificate_name}} is waiting for an administrator: Key Vault {{target_name}}
new_version_held_chain.body:
Alice found a new version of the certificate {{certificate_name}} in the Key Vault {{target_name}}, but its certificate chain is incomplete: a certificate between the website's certificate and the trusted root is missing.

Alice will not deploy this version by itself. An administrator can open the certificate in Alice, check the chain and choose Deploy now, confirming the incomplete chain.

version_skipped_manual.subject: A new version of {{certificate_name}} is not deployed automatically: Key Vault {{target_name}}
version_skipped_manual.body:
A new version of the certificate {{certificate_name}} in the Key Vault {{target_name}} does not meet the rule for automatic deployment: it was created or found before automatic deployment was switched on for this certificate.

Alice will not deploy it by itself and will not mention it again. To deploy it, open the certificate in Alice and choose Deploy now.

version_skipped_disabled.subject: A new version of {{certificate_name}} is disabled: Key Vault {{target_name}}
version_skipped_disabled.body:
A new version of the certificate {{certificate_name}} in the Key Vault {{target_name}} is disabled in Azure, so Alice did not deploy it. The websites keep their current certificate.

Alice will not mention this version again. To use it, enable it in Azure and choose Deploy now in Alice.

version_skipped_expired.subject: A new version of {{certificate_name}} has expired: Key Vault {{target_name}}
version_skipped_expired.body:
A new version of the certificate {{certificate_name}} in the Key Vault {{target_name}} has already expired, so Alice did not deploy it. The websites keep their current certificate.

Alice will not mention this version again. Renew the certificate in Azure; Alice deploys the next version by itself.

version_skipped_not_yet_valid.subject: A new version of {{certificate_name}} is not valid yet: Key Vault {{target_name}}
version_skipped_not_yet_valid.body:
A new version of the certificate {{certificate_name}} in the Key Vault {{target_name}} is not valid yet, so Alice did not deploy it. Browsers would refuse it. The websites keep their current certificate.

Alice will not mention this version again. When it becomes valid, open the certificate in Alice and choose Deploy now.

version_skipped_older.subject: A new version of {{certificate_name}} ends earlier than a certificate in use: Key Vault {{target_name}}
version_skipped_older.body:
A new version of the certificate {{certificate_name}} in the Key Vault {{target_name}} ends earlier than the certificate that at least one connected website serves now, so Alice did not deploy it to that website.

Alice will not mention this version again. If you want it anyway, open the certificate in Alice and choose Deploy now.

version_skipped_superseded.subject: A version of {{certificate_name}} was replaced before it was deployed: Key Vault {{target_name}}
version_skipped_superseded.body:
A new version of the certificate {{certificate_name}} in the Key Vault {{target_name}} was replaced by a newer version before Alice deployed it, so Alice skipped it and deploys the newest version instead.

Alice will not mention this version again.

auto_deploy_untrusted.subject: Automatic deployment of {{certificate_name}} stopped at {{count}} websites: Key Vault {{target_name}}
auto_deploy_untrusted.body:
Alice did not deploy the certificate {{certificate_name}} from the Key Vault {{target_name}} to {{count}} connected websites, because their servers belong to a service that does not accept certificates and keys from the vault's service.

The websites keep their current certificate. Alice deploys there again once a trust allows it.

What to do: an administrator opens Services in Alice, chooses the service of the servers and adds a trust for the vault's service (Trusts), or moves the servers or the vault to the same service.

auto_deploy_stopped.subject: Automatic deployment of {{certificate_name}} stopped: Key Vault {{target_name}}
auto_deploy_stopped.body:
Alice stopped deploying the new version of the certificate {{certificate_name}} from the Key Vault {{target_name}} automatically, after {{count}} deployments failed.

Websites that already received the version keep it; the others keep their current certificate. The deployment history in Alice shows the reason for each failure. Automatic deployment continues with the next version. To try this version again, open the certificate in Alice and choose Deploy now.

import_failed.subject: Importing {{certificate_name}} into the Key Vault {{target_name}} failed
import_failed.body:
Alice could not import the certificate {{certificate_name}} into the Key Vault {{target_name}}. Nothing was created in the vault.

Open the certificate in Alice (Certificates): its import history shows the reason. When it is fixed, start the import again.

import_outcome_unknown.subject: Alice does not know whether {{certificate_name}} was imported into the Key Vault {{target_name}}
import_outcome_unknown.body:
Alice sent the certificate {{certificate_name}} to the Key Vault {{target_name}}, but the answer was lost, and no check of the vault has shown the certificate since. Alice never sends an import twice.

If the vault still exists, open it in Azure and look for the certificate. If it is there, nothing more is needed. If it is not, start the import again in Alice. If the vault was deleted, nothing more is needed.

new_versions_more.subject: More new certificate versions were found in the Key Vault {{target_name}}
new_versions_more.body:
Alice sent a message for each of the first new certificate versions it found in the Key Vault {{target_name}} in one pass. {{count}} more new versions were found in the same pass and are not listed here.

Open the vault in Alice to see the certificates and choose Deploy now where a version should go out.

new_versions_more_one.subject: Another new certificate version was found in the Key Vault {{target_name}}
new_versions_more_one.body:
Alice sent a message for each of the first new certificate versions it found in the Key Vault {{target_name}} in one pass. {{count}} more new version was found in the same pass and is not listed here.

Open the vault in Alice to see the certificate and choose Deploy now if the version should go out.

versions_skipped_more.subject: More certificate versions were not deployed automatically: Key Vault {{target_name}}
versions_skipped_more.body:
Alice sent a message for each of the first certificate versions it did not deploy automatically in the Key Vault {{target_name}} in one pass. {{count}} more versions were skipped in the same pass and are not listed here.

Open the vault in Alice to see them and choose Deploy now where a version should go out.

versions_skipped_more_one.subject: Another certificate version was not deployed automatically: Key Vault {{target_name}}
versions_skipped_more_one.body:
Alice sent a message for each of the first certificate versions it did not deploy automatically in the Key Vault {{target_name}} in one pass. {{count}} more version was skipped in the same pass and is not listed here.

Open the vault in Alice to see it and choose Deploy now if it should go out.

auto_deploys_stopped_more.subject: More automatic deployments stopped: Key Vault {{target_name}}
auto_deploys_stopped_more.body:
Alice sent a message for each of the first certificates whose automatic deployment stopped in the Key Vault {{target_name}} in one pass. {{count}} more stopped in the same pass and are not listed here.

The deployment history in Alice shows the reason for each failure. Choose Deploy now on a certificate's page to try its version again.

auto_deploys_stopped_more_one.subject: Another automatic deployment stopped: Key Vault {{target_name}}
auto_deploys_stopped_more_one.body:
Alice sent a message for each of the first certificates whose automatic deployment stopped in the Key Vault {{target_name}} in one pass. {{count}} more stopped in the same pass and is not listed here.

The deployment history in Alice shows the reason for the failures. Choose Deploy now on the certificate's page to try its version again.

expiry_warning.subject: Alice license expires on {{ends_at}}
expiry_warning.body:
Your Alice license for {{customer}} (license {{license_id}}) expires on {{ends_at}}.

To renew it, send your Installation ID {{installation_id}} to your vendor, then upload the new license file on the License page in Alice. Until then everything keeps working.

evaluation_warning.subject: Alice evaluation ends on {{ends_at}}
evaluation_warning.body:
The 30-day evaluation of Alice ends on {{ends_at}}. After that, Alice pauses automatic tasks and refuses changes to your servers until a license is installed. Your data is kept.

To buy a license, send your Installation ID {{installation_id}} to your vendor.

evaluation_ended.subject: Alice evaluation has ended
evaluation_ended.body:
The evaluation of Alice ended on {{ends_at}}. Automatic tasks are paused and changes to your servers are refused. Your data is safe.

Upload a license on the License page. Your Installation ID is {{installation_id}}.

grace.subject: Alice license expired: automatic tasks stop on {{locks_at}}
grace.body:
Your Alice license {{license_id}} for {{customer}} expired on {{ends_at}}. Everything still works during the 7-day grace period (grace day {{grace_day}} of 7). On {{locks_at}} Alice pauses automatic tasks; only the renewal and automatic deployment of certificates it already manages go on, until {{continuity_ends_at}}.

Contact your vendor now and upload the renewed license on the License page. Your Installation ID is {{installation_id}}.

locked.subject: Alice license expired: automatic tasks are paused
locked.body:
The grace period of your Alice license {{license_id}} ended on {{locks_at}}. Automatic tasks are paused and changes to your servers are refused. Your data is safe, and certificate expiry alerts still arrive by email.

So that your websites do not go down, certificates Alice already manages keep renewing and are still deployed automatically to the places they are bound to until {{continuity_ends_at}} ({{continuity_days_left}} days). After that date this stops too.

Upload a new license on the License page to continue. Your Installation ID is {{installation_id}}.

continuity_ended.subject: Alice license expired: certificates are no longer renewed
continuity_ended.body:
Your Alice license {{license_id}} has expired and its grace period ended on {{locks_at}}. Since {{continuity_ends_at}} Alice no longer renews the certificates it manages and no longer deploys them automatically. Certificates that expire from now on are not replaced, and websites that use them will show errors. Changes to your servers are refused. Your data is safe, and certificate expiry alerts still arrive by email.

Upload a new license on the License page to continue. Your Installation ID is {{installation_id}}.

clock_jump.subject: Alice: the server clock jumped forward
clock_jump.body:
The clock of the Alice server jumped forward by {{jump_days}} days (it now shows {{system_time}}). For the next 24 hours Alice keeps using the previous time for license checks.

If the new time is wrong, correct the server clock. If it is right, nothing needs to be done; you may ask your vendor for a correction license. Your Installation ID is {{installation_id}}.

dead.subject: Alice: a background job failed for good ({{type}})
dead.body:
The background job {{job_id}} ({{type}}) failed after {{attempts}} attempts and will not be retried. The last error code was {{reason}}.

You can see its steps and its error in Alice at /api/v1/jobs/{{job_id}}. If the job was meant to change a server, check that server before you start the work again.

tampered.subject: Alice: a background job was changed outside Alice and was not run ({{type}})
tampered.body:
The background job {{job_id}} ({{type}}) was not run: its stored data failed the integrity check, so it was changed in the database outside Alice. The job is stopped and will not run.

Find out who had direct access to the Alice database. You can see the job at /api/v1/jobs/{{job_id}}.

broken.subject: Alice: the audit log failed its integrity check
broken.body:
The daily check of the Alice audit log found a problem at entry {{first_bad_seq}} ({{problem}}). Entries of the audit log may have been changed or deleted outside Alice.

Keep the database as it is, find out who had direct access to it, and compare the audit log with your latest backup and audit export. Alice keeps recording new entries and checks the log again every hour until it is intact.

renewal_failed.subject: Alice could not renew the certificate for {{name}}
renewal_failed.body:
Alice tried to renew the certificate for {{names}} {{count}} times in a row and did not succeed.

Reason of the last attempt: {{reason}}

The current certificate stays in use and keeps working until {{expires_at}}. Alice keeps trying by itself and waits longer between the attempts, at most a day, and less as that time nears. If the cause is a temporary outage (the certificate authority or the DNS service cannot be reached, does not answer in time or limits the requests), Alice keeps trying until the certificate is renewed. If the cause needs a person (for example a setting, the account at the certificate authority or a refused name), Alice stops after 5 such failures.

What to do: open Issued certificates in Alice and choose this certificate. Its page shows the reason of each attempt and whether it looks temporary. Remove the cause, then choose Order now to renew it at once.

auto_renew_stopped.subject: Automatic renewal stopped: certificate for {{name}}
auto_renew_stopped.body:
Alice stopped renewing the certificate for {{names}} by itself after {{count}} failed attempts in a row, because the cause needs a person (or the certificate has already expired).

Reason of the last attempt: {{reason}}

The current certificate stays in use until {{expires_at}}. After that time, visitors of the websites that use it see a security warning. While renewal stays stopped, Alice reminds you 14, 7, 3 and 1 days before that time.

What to do: open Issued certificates in Alice and choose this certificate. Its page shows the reason of each attempt. Remove the cause, then an administrator chooses Check again and resume: Alice orders the certificate at once and renews it by itself again. Order now also renews it at once; when that succeeds, Alice renews it by itself again.

renewal_expiring_transient.subject: Certificate for {{name}} expires soon and its renewal is failing (days left: {{days}})
renewal_expiring_transient.body:
The certificate for {{names}} ends at {{expires_at}}. Days left: {{days}}. Alice has not been able to renew it: {{count}} attempts in a row failed.

Reason of the last attempt: {{reason}}

This looks like a temporary outage: the certificate authority or the DNS service could not be reached, did not answer in time or limited the requests. Alice keeps trying by itself, more often as the end nears.

What to do: check that Alice can reach the certificate authority and the DNS service. Open Issued certificates in Alice and choose this certificate: its page shows each attempt. An administrator can choose Check again and resume to try at once.

renewal_expiring_permanent.subject: Certificate for {{name}} expires soon and its renewal needs attention (days left: {{days}})
renewal_expiring_permanent.body:
The certificate for {{names}} ends at {{expires_at}}. Days left: {{days}}. Alice has not been able to renew it: {{count}} attempts in a row failed.

Reason of the last attempt: {{reason}}

This cause is not expected to go away by itself: for example a setting, the account at the certificate authority, a refused name or a wrong answer to the check of the names. Alice tries a few more times and stops after 5 such failures.

What to do: open Issued certificates in Alice and choose this certificate. Its page shows the reason of each attempt. Remove the cause, then an administrator chooses Check again and resume, so that Alice orders the certificate at once.

renewal_expiring_stopped.subject: Certificate for {{name}} expires soon and is no longer renewed automatically (days left: {{days}})
renewal_expiring_stopped.body:
The certificate for {{names}} ends at {{expires_at}}. Days left: {{days}}. Alice stopped renewing it by itself after {{count}} failed attempts in a row, because the cause needs a person. Alice does not try again by itself.

Reason of the last attempt: {{reason}}

After {{expires_at}}, visitors of the websites that use the certificate see a security warning.

What to do: open Issued certificates in Alice and choose this certificate. Its page shows the reason of each attempt. Remove the cause, then an administrator chooses Check again and resume, so that Alice orders the certificate at once and renews it by itself again.

renewal_ca_wait.subject: The certificate authority asked Alice to wait before renewing the certificate for {{name}} (days left: {{days}})
renewal_ca_wait.body:
The certificate authority limited the requests for the certificate for {{names}} and asked Alice not to order it again before {{ca_not_before}}. The current certificate ends at {{expires_at}}. Days left: {{days}}. Alice has tried {{count}} times in a row.

Reason of the last attempt: {{reason}}

Alice waits until then and orders the certificate again by itself afterwards; ordering sooner only makes the wait longer. Little time is left after this wait to renew the certificate before it ends.

What to do: find out why the authority limits the requests (for example too many certificates for the same names, or too many failed checks) and keep the limit from recurring. If the certificate cannot wait, get one from another certificate authority and upload it to Alice. Open Issued certificates in Alice and choose this certificate: its page shows when the authority accepts orders again.

auto_deploy_untrusted.subject: Automatic deployment stopped at {{count}} websites: certificate for {{name}}
auto_deploy_untrusted.body:
Alice did not put the certificate for {{names}} on {{count}} bound websites by itself, because their servers belong to a service that does not accept certificates and keys from the certificate's service.

The websites keep their current certificate. Alice deploys there again once a trust allows it.

What to do: an administrator opens Services in Alice, chooses the service of the servers and adds a trust for the certificate's service (Trusts), or moves the servers or the certificate to the same service.

auto_deploy_stopped.subject: Automatic deployment stopped: certificate for {{name}}
auto_deploy_stopped.body:
Alice stopped putting the new certificate for {{names}} on its websites by itself, because {{count}} deployments of it failed.

Reason of the last failed deployment: {{reason}}

Websites that already received the new certificate keep it; the others keep their current certificate. The deployment history in Alice shows the result of each deployment: where Alice could not confirm that the earlier certificate was put back, the history says so and the website needs a check.

What to do: open Issued certificates in Alice and choose this certificate. Its page lists the websites and the result of each deployment. Remove the cause, then choose Deploy now. The next certificate Alice gets for these names is deployed by itself again.

auto_deploy_held_license.subject: New certificate for {{name}} is waiting for an administrator
auto_deploy_held_license.body:
Alice got a new certificate for {{names}} before its license last started to allow changes again (after a time in which it did not), and the certificate has not been deployed anywhere yet. Alice does not put such a certificate on the websites by itself, so that a person looks at it first.

The websites keep the certificate they have now.

What to do: open Issued certificates in Alice and choose this certificate. Check it, then choose Deploy now, or release it so that Alice deploys it by itself.

auto_deploy_held_chain.subject: New certificate for {{name}} needs a check before it is deployed
auto_deploy_held_chain.body:
Alice got a new certificate for {{names}}, but Alice cannot confirm that the certificates that vouch for it reach a certificate authority it trusts. Alice does not put such a certificate on the websites by itself, because some visitors might see a security warning.

The websites keep the certificate they have now.

What to do: an administrator opens Issued certificates in Alice and chooses this certificate. If the certificate authority's own certificate is missing, add it to the certificate authority's settings. Otherwise check the certificate and choose Deploy now with the confirmation.

nothing_to_rotate.subject: Planned SSH key rotation found nothing it could change: {{key_label}}
nothing_to_rotate.body:
The scheduled rotation of the SSH key {{key_label}} ({{fingerprint}}) did not start, because every place where the key is used is skipped. Places skipped: {{skip_count}}. Servers and skip reasons: {{skips}}.

The troubleshooting guide explains each skip reason in its section "SSH key rotation"; often scanning the server again is enough. This interval's run is skipped; the next run is planned for {{next_run_at}}.

late_result.subject: Late answer in the SSH key rotation: {{key_label}}
late_result.body:
After the rotation of {{key_label}} had given up on one place, the server answered. Server: {{server}}. User: {{os_user}}. File: {{file_path}}.

Result: {{result}} (removed: the old key is no longer there; undone: the new key is no longer there).

Alice queued a scan of the server so that its key list shows the file as it is now. Open the rotation's page in Alice to check this place.

preview.subject: Planned SSH key rotation: {{key_label}}
preview.body:
Alice plans to rotate the SSH key {{key_label}} ({{fingerprint}}). Planned start: {{planned_for}}. A policy that is switched off starts a run only when an administrator chooses Run now.

Alice will add a new key next to the old one, check that the new key works, keep both keys for the overlap, then remove the old key. Nothing is removed where the new key did not work.

Places that will change: {{change_count}}. Places that will be skipped: {{skip_count}}.

Open the key's page in Alice to see the exact servers, users and files. To stop a planned run, switch the policy off before it starts.

preview_after_license.subject: SSH key rotation can continue after the license renewal: {{key_label}}
preview_after_license.body:
The license allows changes again. The rotation of the SSH key {{key_label}} ({{fingerprint}}), which was paused while the license did not allow changes, continues only after an administrator chooses Continue on the rotation's page.

Before Alice removes the old key anywhere, it signs in with the new key again on that server. Where this fails, the old key stays.

Places this rotation changes: {{change_count}}. Open the rotation's page in Alice to see them.

overlap_started.subject: New SSH key ready: {{key_label}}
overlap_started.body:
The new key for {{key_label}} works on every server where Alice could check it (new fingerprint: {{new_fingerprint}}). The old and the new key are both valid until {{overlap_until}}. Then Alice removes the old key where the new key works, after checking the new key once more.

If people or systems use this key outside Alice, an administrator can download the new private key now from the new key's page in Alice.

overlap_ending.subject: The old SSH key will be removed soon: {{key_label}}
overlap_ending.body: At {{overlap_until}} Alice removes the old key {{key_label}} from the servers where the new key works, after checking the new key once more. If something still uses the old key, an administrator should download the new private key now.

completed.subject: SSH key rotation finished: {{key_label}}
completed.body: Alice removed the old key {{key_label}} from every server where the new key works. The new key (fingerprint {{new_fingerprint}}) is now the key the policy rotates. Alice keeps the old private key, encrypted, for 30 days after the old key is no longer used anywhere, then destroys it.

completed_partial.subject: SSH key rotation finished, but the old key still works in some places: {{key_label}}
completed_partial.body:
Alice removed the old key {{key_label}} wherever the new key works and was checked once more. The new key (fingerprint {{new_fingerprint}}) is now the key the policy rotates.

The old key is still valid in places the rotation skipped and in places where an administrator chose to keep it. Places where the old key stays: {{kept_count}}. Later rotations do not return to them.

Open the old key's page in Alice to see these places, and remove the old key there when nothing uses it any more.

aborted.subject: SSH key rotation undone: {{key_label}}
aborted.body:
The rotation of {{key_label}} did not finish, so Alice removed the new key again where it had added it. The old key was not touched anywhere and keeps working.

Reason code: {{code}}. The troubleshooting guide explains it, and the rotation's page in Alice shows each server's state.

needs_attention.subject: SSH key rotation needs attention: {{key_label}}
needs_attention.body:
The rotation of {{key_label}} has a problem a person must look at. Alice removes the old key only where a login with the new key worked just before; everywhere else the old key stays. Where Alice could not remove the new key again, both keys are there.

Reason code: {{code}}. The troubleshooting guide explains it. Servers where the new key may still be present because removing it again failed: {{undo_failed_servers}} (count: {{undo_failed_count}}).

Servers where the old key stays because removing it failed: {{remove_failed_servers}} (count: {{remove_failed_count}}).

Open the rotation's page in Alice to see each server's state.

paused_license.subject: SSH key rotation paused: {{key_label}}
paused_license.body:
The license has expired or could not be checked, so Alice paused the rotation of {{key_label}}. The old key stays in place: Alice adds no new key and removes no old key. If the rotation was in its overlap, the overlap stops counting and its remaining time resumes after Continue.

When the license is valid again, an administrator must choose Continue on the rotation's page.

decision_needed.subject: SSH key rotation waits for a decision: {{key_label}}
decision_needed.body: Alice added the new key for {{key_label}} but could not test a login with it in some places (count: {{count}}). On the rotation's page, decide whether to keep the old key there or to stop and undo the rotation. Without a decision Alice undoes the rotation at {{decision_due}} (later if the rotation is paused because of the license).

skip.connection_files_unknown: Alice does not know all key files of the account it connects with on this server; scan the server again.
skip.connection_account_file: This place belongs to the account Alice connects with or to one of its files; Alice never changes those.
skip.target_deleted: The server was removed from Alice.
skip.host_key_unconfirmed: The server's fingerprint is not confirmed yet.
skip.target_not_connected: Alice cannot connect to the server right now.
skip.keys_managed_elsewhere: The server gets this user's keys from a program.
skip.sshd_unreadable: Alice could not read the SSH server settings.
skip.connection_account: This is the account Alice connects with.
skip.missing: The key was no longer found here.
skip.cert_authority: This line is a certificate authority.
skip.shared_file_skipped: Several users of this server read this file, so Alice does not change the key in it.
skip.pubkey_disabled: The SSH server does not accept keys.
skip.root_forced_commands_only: root may sign in here only with a fixed command, and this line has none.
skip.duplicate_lines: The key is listed more than once in this file.
skip.options_unreadable: Alice could not read this line's options exactly.
skip.options_truncated: This line's options are longer than Alice stores, so Alice cannot copy them to the new key.
